items.title: native — a FIELD named `self` or `super` is emitted as `r#self`/`r#super`, which rustc REFUSES (raw identifiers cannot spell those two) — live today; the emitter must mangle instead of raw-quoting
items.body: Pin: a struct with a `self` field builds and runs natively byte-identical with JS; the mangling rule written where the emitter names fields. Sizing S; native lane.

items.title: `[derive(Wire)]` binds a LOCAL per field, so a field named `deserializer` (or any name the expansion itself uses) fails with 5 errors (`json.vl:995`, `rpc.vl:5692`) — the derive's hygiene: its own locals must not collide with field names
items.body: Fix: the expansion's locals take a spelling no user identifier can (a reserved prefix), or the derive reads fields through positional accessors. Pin: a `deserializer` field round-trips. Sizing S.

items.title: a METHOD named `Self` is accepted at its declaration but cannot be called (`x.Self()` parses `Self` as the type); refuse the name at the declaration with a steer
items.body: One parser rule + ledger row. Sizing XS.

items.title: the lexical spec §2.2's contextual-keyword list OMITS `as` and `only`, which the compiler already treats as contextual (accepted as names at every position probed); `layer` is listed nowhere and is not a word the compiler knows
items.body: Add `as`/`only` to §2.2's list; drop `layer` from any list that names it. Gates grammar_ebnf/grammar_sync if the EBNF carries the list. Sizing XS; may ride syntax-42's EBNF pass.

items.title: bindgen's `RESERVED` list has DRIFTED from the lexer: it lacks `css`, `dyn` and `lazy`, so a TypeScript member named one of those produces bindings that do not parse — the list should be derived from the lexer's `KEYWORDS` (one source), and after B413 it must not name `resource`
items.body: Fix: `RESERVED` = the lexer's table (a shared constant or a pin that they agree); a pin per drifted word. Sizing S.
